survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive results for Indonesia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically relies on sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and correct standard errors. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., student design weights or replicate weights), so analysts should use the official PISA 2022 weight variables provided in the OECD database for any re-analysis. Because this document is a reporting factsheet rather than an ML modeling paper, it does not describe any custom weighting or replicate-weight procedure beyond the standard PISA technical standards.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This factsheet does not present an empirical student-level predictive model and does not describe any plausible-values (PV) estimation or combining procedure. The reported outcomes are PISA performance levels and mean performance summaries derived from the OECD PISA scaling framework, not from an ML pipeline that would require explicit PV and missing-data handling documentation in the text. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported at the level of an analysis method because the document is a descriptive results product rather than a methodological study.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is the set of students in Indonesia who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, administered as two subject tests with different booklets and subject combinations. The factsheet reports that 13,439 students in 410 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science in Indonesia; it also states that all data met PISA quality standards for reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 results for Indonesia, reporting trends and cross-sectional comparisons in mathematics, reading, and science for 15-year-old students. It describes that students took two two-hour tests, with different students receiving different test questions and subject combinations, and that students also completed a background questionnaire while school principals completed a school questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance trends (e.g., declines from 2018 to 2022), proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2 and Level 5/6), and subgroup patterns such as socioeconomic gradients (ESCS quintiles) and gender differences. It also provides contextual indicators on school belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety and bullying, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. No student-level machine learning models are estimated in this document; therefore, no predictive metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) are applicable, and causal interpretation is not supported by the factsheet’s descriptive design.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not specify an ML research design, does not evaluate predictive algorithms, and does not report PV-combining or missing-data imputation procedures as part of an analysis pipeline. The absence of ML techniques and main findings is consistent with the document’s purpose: to communicate benchmarked performance levels and contextual patterns using the OECD PISA scaling and reporting framework.
